na8021c13edd.s: Which districts carry most of Andhra Pradesh's malaria and scrub typhus burden?
na8021c13edd.x: The agency or tribal districts carry most of Andhra Pradesh's malaria and scrub typhus burden, making them a priority for surveillance and control.

nbiology-18-14.s: Humans become hosts of the Guinea worm (Dracunculus medinensis) mainly by:
nbiology-18-14.x: Guinea worm larvae develop in Cyclops, and people who drink water containing infected Cyclops become hosts of the worm.

n2da62587d7e.s: Which of the following diseases spreads through the faecal-oral route by contaminated water or food?
n2da62587d7e.x: The faecal-oral group includes cholera, typhoid, hepatitis A and E, acute diarrhoea, dysentery and polio; hepatitis B, dengue and rabies spread otherwise.

nbiology-21-8.s: Schistosomiasis, common in developing countries, is chiefly associated with:
nbiology-21-8.x: Schistosomiasis spreads through water contaminated by infected snails and excreta, so it is common where water and sanitation are unsafe.

nbiology-15-36.s: Rinderpest, a disease of cattle and buffalo, was declared globally eradicated in:
nbiology-15-36.x: Rinderpest affected cattle and buffalo until it was declared globally eradicated in 2011.

nd0cf777f058.s: About how many scrub typhus cases did Andhra Pradesh report in 2026?
nd0cf777f058.x: Scrub typhus accounted for 941 cases and was rising in ASR and Parvathipuram Manyam districts.

n079be90d1b7.s: How many species of Plasmodium are recognised as infecting humans?
n079be90d1b7.x: Five species infect humans: P. falciparum, P. vivax, P. malariae, P. ovale and P. knowlesi.

nadb989692b1.s: Which bacterium controls mosquito-borne disease through cytoplasmic incompatibility and pathogen blocking?
nadb989692b1.x: Wolbachia is a bacterium associated with cytoplasmic incompatibility and pathogen blocking; Gambusia and guppy are larvivorous fish.

nb81a18e2324.s: According to WHO, ambient outdoor air pollution caused about how many premature deaths in 2019?
nb81a18e2324.x: The WHO estimate is 4.2 million premature deaths from ambient outdoor air pollution in 2019.

n7292f41085c.s: Hearing loss, hypertension, sleep disorders and anxiety are health effects of:
n7292f41085c.x: Noise pollution is associated with hearing loss, hypertension, sleep disorders and anxiety; arsenic, cadmium and fluoride cause blackfoot, itai-itai and fluorosis.

na498d5808c5.s: Which of the following practices promotes antimicrobial resistance?
na498d5808c5.x: Self-medication is a driver of AMR; it is unregulated, not supervised, veterinary drug use and incomplete courses that promote resistance.

ndce9911c126.s: Which of the following is in the critical-priority group of the WHO Bacterial Priority Pathogens List, 2024?
ndce9911c126.x: The critical-priority group includes carbapenem-resistant A. baumannii, Enterobacterales and rifampicin-resistant TB.

n5e3ff9ee6b4.s: India's life expectancy rose from 49.7 years in 1973 to about how many years in 2023?
n5e3ff9ee6b4.x: Life expectancy rose from 49.7 to 70.3 years, yet NCDs cause over 57% of deaths while communicable diseases persist - a double burden.

nbiology-66-12.s: Biofilms contribute to persistent or chronic infection mainly because their EPS matrix:
o: Protects microbes and reduces antibiotic penetration
nbiology-66-12.x: The EPS matrix shields biofilm microbes and blocks antibiotics, so infections persist.

nbiology-43-5.s: Biofilms can form on which of the following?
o: Implants, tissues, food and food-processing surfaces
nbiology-43-5.x: Biofilms grow on medical implants, human tissues, food and food-processing surfaces.

nbiology-66-7.s: Which of the following can generate antibiotic resistance in bacteria?
nbiology-66-7.x: Mutation can generate resistance; antibiotic use in livestock and repeated exposure also select resistant organisms.

nbiology-66-8.s: Not completing a course of antibiotics promotes antimicrobial resistance because:
o: Resistant survivors are left to multiply
nbiology-66-8.x: Stopping a course early lets resistant survivors multiply, which is how it promotes resistance.

n380c6e36c41.s: How many diseases are covered under the National Center for Vector Borne Diseases Control (NCVBDC)?
n380c6e36c41.x: NCVBDC covers six diseases: malaria, Japanese encephalitis, dengue, chikungunya, kala-azar and lymphatic filariasis - not TB.

nbd9e82d5d89.s: DALY (Disability-Adjusted Life Year) is the sum of:
o: YLL and years gained through treatment
nbd9e82d5d89.x: DALY = YLL (years of life lost) + YLD (years lived with disability); it does not add years gained through treatment.

nb4687ca7e05.s: According to WHO, which is the world's single biggest killer?
nb4687ca7e05.x: WHO identifies ischaemic heart disease as the world's single biggest killer, while cardiovascular diseases lead in India.

n7ad05ecda51.s: Which of the following is a main risk factor for lifestyle (non-communicable) diseases?
n7ad05ecda51.x: Unhealthy diet, physical inactivity, tobacco and alcohol are the main NCD risk factors.

nab656dc05eb.s: The UN General Assembly declaration on NCDs and mental health calls for what regarding e-cigarettes?
nab656dc05eb.x: The declaration calls for stronger, not relaxed, regulation of tobacco, trans fats and e-cigarettes.

nbiology-28-11.s: Butyric acid is a fatty acid mainly associated with:
nbiology-28-11.x: Butter is known for butyric acid; linseed gives alpha-linolenic acid and macadamia nuts palmitoleic acid.

n4839a4210d6.s: A major plague outbreak hit Surat, Gujarat, in which year?
n4839a4210d6.x: Plague, caused by Yersinia pestis, hit Surat in 1994.

nbiology-70-7.x: A live attenuated vaccine uses a weakened living pathogen; killed pathogens are used in inactivated vaccines.

nbiology-70-21.x: Inactivated vaccines use a killed pathogen; a genetically engineered antigen protein is the recombinant platform.

nbiology-70-15.x: Smallpox is caused by variola virus.

ncc368deb190.s: During COVID-19, Andhra Pradesh added COVID treatment to which scheme?
ncc368deb190.x: Andhra Pradesh covered COVID treatment under Aarogyasri, alongside volunteer fever surveys and the Covid Pharma app.

ne492522c153.s: The Lancet report of 24 February 2022 estimated that about how many children in India lost a parent or caregiver to COVID-19?
ne492522c153.x: The report estimated about 19 lakh children lost a parent or caregiver.

nc20d77d6d31.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about India's COVID-19 strategy?
o: It relied on a single-tier facility arrangement
It set up MHA Empowered Groups
nc20d77d6d31.x: India used a three-tier, not single-tier, facility arrangement along with test-track-treat-vaccinate, COVID-appropriate behaviour and MHA Empowered Groups.

new.s: MERA India (Malaria Elimination Research Alliance), launched in April 2019, is an initiative of:
new.x: MERA India was launched by ICMR on 24 April 2019 and is steered by ICMR-NIMR, New Delhi.

new.s: Maldives was certified malaria-free by WHO in:
new.x: WHO certified Maldives malaria-free in 2015 and Sri Lanka in 2016.

new.s: Under NCVBDC, which disease is targeted only for control, not elimination?
new.x: Malaria, LF and kala-azar are targeted for elimination; dengue, chikungunya and JE are only controlled.

new.s: The Red Line campaign (2016) puts a red line on the packs of:
new.x: The Red Line campaign marks prescription-only antibiotics to curb their misuse.

new.s: India's One Health based National Action Plan on AMR (NAP-AMR) was launched in:
new.x: NAP-AMR came in 2017; the Red Line campaign was 2016 and Kerala's KARSAP 2018.

new.s: Which State was the first to adopt its own action plan on antimicrobial resistance (KARSAP, 2018)?
new.x: Kerala's KARSAP (2018) was the first State AMR action plan.

new.s: Nafithromycin (Miqnaf), launched in November 2024, is India's first indigenous:
new.x: Nafithromycin is the first indigenous macrolide, for community-acquired pneumonia, by Wockhardt with BIRAC.

new.s: Which was the first anti-TB drug?
new.x: Waksman found streptomycin, the first anti-TB drug; penicillin was Fleming's discovery.

new.s: The Integrated Disease Surveillance Programme (IDSP), launched in 2004, is run by:
new.x: IDSP is run by the Health Ministry through NCDC and uses the IHIP digital platform.

new.s: The digital platform used by IDSP is:
new.x: IDSP reports through the IHIP digital platform; U-WIN registers UIP vaccinations.

new.s: How many sections does the Epidemic Diseases Act, 1897 have?
new.x: The Epidemic Diseases Act, 1897 has 4 sections.

new.s: The Epidemic Diseases Act, 1897 was amended in 2020 mainly to:
new.x: The 2020 amendment protects health workers.

new.s: The National Institute of One Health is located at:
new.x: The National Institute of One Health is at Nagpur.

new.s: Mission Indradhanush aims at full immunisation of more than what share of children and pregnant women?
new.x: Mission Indradhanush (Dec 2014) targets over 90% full immunisation.

new.s: The Universal Immunisation Programme, which covered 6 diseases at launch in 1985, now covers:
new.x: UIP started with 6 diseases and now covers 12.

new.s: Which of the following is NOT among the diseases covered under the Universal Immunisation Programme?
new.x: UIP's 12 diseases include rotavirus, JE and rubella, but not malaria.

new.s: WHO projects about 2.5 lakh extra climate-linked deaths a year (2030-2050). Which cause accounts for the most?
new.x: Child undernutrition (95,000) leads, followed by malaria (60,000), diarrhoea (48,000) and heat (38,000).

new.s: In 2022, what share of human infectious diseases were found to be aggravated by climate hazards?
new.x: 58% (218 of 375) human infectious diseases are aggravated by climate hazards.

new.s: Global warming raises the risk of dengue and malaria mainly by:
o: Expanding the range of their vectors
new.x: Warming expands the range of dengue and malaria vectors.

new.s: Heatwaves are chiefly linked with:
new.x: Heatwaves cause dehydration, heatstroke and cardiovascular stress; leptospirosis follows floods.

new.s: Malaria cases in Andhra Pradesh in 2026 (to 30 August) rose by 27.9% to about:
new.x: Malaria rose to 7,895 cases in 2026 (to 30 August), with hotspots in ASR, Polavaram and Vizianagaram.

new.s: Andhra Pradesh reported about how many dengue cases in 2026 (to 30 August)?
new.x: Dengue stood at 1,475 cases in 2026 (to 30 August).

new.s: Mpox virus was first isolated (DR Congo, 1985) from a:
new.x: Mpox comes from rodents and was first isolated from a rope squirrel in DR Congo in 1985.

new.s: Kyasanur Forest Disease spreads to humans from monkeys through:
new.x: KFD is a monkey-associated disease spread by ticks.

new.s: The natural reservoir of the Nipah virus is the:
new.x: Fruit bats (Pteropus) are Nipah's reservoir; pigs are the intermediate host.

new.s: About how many children die daily worldwide from preventable water- and sanitation-related diseases?
new.x: About 5,000 children die daily from preventable water- and sanitation-related disease.

new.s: Which water-borne disease is the leading child killer?
new.x: Acute diarrhoea (rotavirus, E. coli, Shigella) is the leading child killer.

new.s: Which of the following contaminant–disease pairs is correctly matched?
new.x: Mercury causes Minamata disease; cadmium causes itai-itai, arsenic blackfoot and nitrate blue-baby syndrome.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about hepatitis:
1. Hepatitis A and E are water-borne.
2. Hepatitis B has no vaccine.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Hepatitis A and E spread faeco-orally; hepatitis B is blood-borne and has a vaccine, so 2 is wrong.

new.s: Smallpox, the only disease eradicated in India, was eradicated in:
new.x: India eradicated smallpox in 1977; 2011 is the global eradication of rinderpest.

new.s: Adding injuries such as road accidents to communicable and non-communicable diseases gives the:
new.x: The triple burden adds injuries to CDs and NCDs.

new.s: The coexistence of undernutrition and obesity is called the:
new.x: Undernutrition plus obesity is the dual burden of malnutrition, not the dual burden of disease.

new.s: The India State-Level Disease Burden Initiative is part of which global study?
new.x: The initiative (ICMR, PHFI, IHME) is part of the Global Burden of Disease study.

new.s: In Omran's theory of epidemiological transition, the last stage is the Age of:
new.x: Omran's three stages end with the Age of Degenerative and Man-Made Diseases, when NCDs dominate.

new.s: The 'Nations within a nation' study (Lancet, 2017) placed Indian States in how many Epidemiological Transition Level groups?
new.x: It used 4 ETL groups: low, lower-middle, higher-middle and high.

new.s: Which of the following States is in the high Epidemiological Transition Level group?
new.x: Kerala, Goa, Tamil Nadu and Punjab are high ETL; Karnataka and Delhi are higher-middle.

new.s: A high Epidemiological Transition Level means:
o: A more advanced transition, with NCDs dominating
new.x: A low ratio of communicable to NCD-plus-injury DALYs gives a high ETL: the transition is more advanced.

new.s: For India as a whole, NCD and injury DALYs overtook communicable-disease DALYs in:
new.x: NCD + injury DALYs overtook communicable DALYs in 2003.

new.s: Since 1990, India's maternal mortality ratio has fallen by about:
new.x: MMR has fallen 86% and under-five mortality 78% since 1990.

new.s: Since 1990, India's under-five mortality has fallen by about:
new.x: Under-five mortality has fallen 78%; MMR fell 86%.

new.s: According to the Economic Survey 2025-26, NCDs account for what share of all deaths in India?
new.x: NCDs account for 57% of all deaths in India.

new.s: Which of the following is a communicable disease?
new.x: Chikungunya is pathogen-caused; diabetes, hypertension and COPD are lifestyle diseases.

new.s: In 2026, ICMR expanded wastewater surveillance from 5 cities to:
new.x: ICMR's wastewater surveillance expanded from 5 to 50 cities, tracking 10 viruses and AMR.

new.s: ICMR's expanded wastewater surveillance tracks how many viruses, including avian influenza?
new.x: It tracks 10 viruses, including avian influenza, plus AMR.

new.s: Which ICMR initiative is aimed at malaria elimination?
new.x: MERA is the malaria elimination alliance; the India TB Research Consortium targets TB.

new.s: According to NFHS-5 (2019-21), what share of women in India are overweight or obese?
new.x: NFHS-5 found 24% of women and 23% of men overweight or obese.

new.s: According to ICMR-INDIAB (2023), the prevalence of diabetes in India is:
new.x: Diabetes prevalence is 11.4% (~101 million); 15.3% is prediabetes.

new.s: According to ICMR-INDIAB (2023), the prevalence of hypertension in India is about:
new.x: Hypertension prevalence is 35.5% (~315 million).

new.s: India's cancer cases (1.41 million in 2022) are projected to reach about how many by 2045?
new.x: Cancer cases are projected to rise to 2.46 million by 2045.

new.s: Which State most recently made cancer a notifiable disease (July 2026)?
new.x: Telangana is the latest of the 17 States that have notified cancer.

new.s: According to GBD 2017, about how many Indians suffered from mental disorders?
new.x: 197.3 million Indians, about 1 in 7, had mental disorders in 2017.

new.s: The most common mental disorder in India (GBD 2017) was:
new.x: Depressive disorders (45.7 million) were most common, just ahead of anxiety disorders (44.9 million).

new.s: According to MoRTH, road accidents in India in 2022 caused about how many deaths?
new.x: There were 4,61,312 accidents and 1,68,491 deaths in 2022.

new.s: Which group formed the largest share of road-accident victims in India in 2022?
new.x: Two-wheeler users were the largest group of road-accident victims.

new.s: Under NP-NCD, Centre-State funding for general States is shared in the ratio:
new.x: NP-NCD funding is 60:40, and 90:10 for North-Eastern and hilly States.

new.s: SDG 3 aims to cut premature deaths from NCDs by:
new.x: SDG 3 seeks a one-third cut in premature NCD deaths and to halve road-traffic deaths.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about NP-NCD:
1. It was formerly NPCDCS, launched in 2010.
2. It screens everyone above 40 years.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: NP-NCD (formerly NPCDCS, 2010) screens everyone above 30, not 40.

new.s: Andhra Pradesh's first Diabetic Foot and Ulcer Clinic (July 2026) was opened at:
new.x: AP's first Diabetic Foot and Ulcer Clinic is at Vizianagaram.

new.s: How many AES/JE cases did Andhra Pradesh report in 2025?
new.x: AES/JE had 146 cases in 2025; 52 was chikungunya, 2,686 dengue and 7,119 malaria.

new.s: An epidemic among animals is called:
new.x: Epizootic is an epidemic among animals; endemic means constant presence.

new.s: A disease always present at a steady level in a place or group is:
new.x: Endemic means constantly present; an epidemic is a sudden outbreak.

new.s: The Ebola virus belongs to which family?
new.x: Ebola is a filovirus (Filoviridae), not a coronavirus.

new.s: WHO declared H1N1 'swine flu' a pandemic in:
new.x: WHO declared the H1N1 pandemic in June 2009.

new.s: In the 2014-16 West African Ebola outbreak, which country was affected first?
new.x: Guinea was hit first, then Sierra Leone and Liberia, the worst hit.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about WHO declarations:
1. COVID-19 was declared a PHEIC on 30 January 2020.
2. The 2026 Bundibugyo Ebola outbreak was declared a pandemic emergency.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: COVID-19 became a PHEIC on 30 January 2020; the 2026 Bundibugyo Ebola outbreak is a PHEIC, not a pandemic emergency.

new.s: In the name 'COVID-19', the number 19 refers to:
new.x: COVID-19 means 'Coronavirus Disease 2019'.

new.s: The Omicron variant of SARS-CoV-2 was first found in:
new.x: Omicron was first found in southern Africa; Delta in India and Alpha in the UK.

new.s: Which animal is the suspected intermediate host of SARS-CoV-2?
new.x: Bats are the reservoir and pangolins the suspected intermediate host; civets were linked to SARS.

new.s: India crossed 200 crore COVID-19 vaccine doses on:
new.x: India reached 200 crore doses on 17 July 2022; vaccination began on 16 January 2021.

new.s: The Delta-driven second wave of COVID-19 in India came in:
new.x: The Delta second wave was in April-May 2021; Omicron drove the third wave in January 2022.

new.s: CoWIN was used mainly for:
o: Vaccine booking, tracking and digital certificates
Tracking OTC sales of fever medicines
new.x: CoWIN handled vaccine booking, tracking and digital certificates.

new.s: Sputnik V (Gam-COVID-Vac) was developed by:
new.x: Sputnik V is an adenovirus-vector vaccine from the Gamaleya Institute, Russia.

new.s: The Moderna COVID-19 vaccine is based on which platform?
new.x: Moderna and Pfizer-BioNTech are mRNA vaccines.

new.s: Which of the following vaccine–platform pairs is correctly matched?
new.x: Corbevax is a protein subunit vaccine; Covaxin is inactivated, Covishield a viral vector and ZyCoV-D a DNA vaccine.

new.s: 'Vaccine Maitri' refers to:
o: India's vaccine supply to low- and middle-income countries
new.x: Vaccine Maitri is India's own vaccine supply initiative; COVAX was co-led by WHO, Gavi and CEPI.

new.s: The 'Break the Chain' COVID-19 campaign belonged to:
new.x: Break the Chain was Kerala's; Mo Jeeban was Odisha's and the Dharavi model Maharashtra's.

new.s: The Chandipura outbreak in Gujarat (2024) is spread by:
new.x: Chandipura, like kala-azar, is spread by the sandfly, not a mosquito.

new.s: Which State had a Zika outbreak in 2021?
new.x: Kerala had a Zika outbreak in 2021; Zika is spread by Aedes.

new.s: Which of the following is a digital health tool highlighted among the lessons of COVID-19?
new.x: Digital tools such as CoWIN, U-WIN, ABDM and eSanjeevani were key lessons; the others are containment models or insurance.

new.s: By October 2020, Andhra Pradesh had crossed how many COVID-19 tests per million?
new.x: AP had the highest tests per million among large States, crossing 1 lakh per million by October 2020.

new.s: Which of the following diseases is NOT spread by a mosquito?
new.x: Scrub typhus is spread by the chigger mite; Zika, West Nile and chikungunya are mosquito-borne.

new.s: Which of the following is NOT a zoonotic disease?
new.x: Mucormycosis is a fungal infection that is not zoonotic; rabies, Nipah and anthrax come from animals.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about Nafithromycin:
1. It was developed by Wockhardt with BIRAC.
2. It was developed by Sun Pharma.
3. It treats community-acquired pneumonia.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Nafithromycin is by Wockhardt with BIRAC, not Sun Pharma, and treats community-acquired pneumonia.

new.s: Which of the following is NOT a lifestyle (non-communicable) disease?
new.x: Typhoid is a pathogen-caused communicable disease; stroke, COPD and obesity are lifestyle diseases.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about trans fat:
1. It raises LDL cholesterol.
2. It raises HDL cholesterol.
3. FSSAI caps it at 2% in fats and oils.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Trans fat raises LDL and lowers HDL; FSSAI caps it at 2%.

new.s: Which of the following outbreak–State pairs is NOT correct?
new.x: Chandipura broke out in Gujarat (2024); plague hit Surat, Gujarat, bird flu first came at Navapur, Maharashtra, and Nipah in Kerala.

new.s: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched?
new.x: Covaxin is an inactivated whole-virus vaccine; Covishield and Sputnik V are viral-vector vaccines.
